html:
Guinea is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, with its capital at Conakry. In 1958 it became the first French colony in Africa to vote itself free.

The Niger River rises in its highlands, and the old heartland of the Mali Empire reached into its east. In the 1700s a Fula jihad built an Islamic state in the Futa Jallon hills. Samori Touré fought France across the region until his capture in 1898. Guinea then became part of French West Africa.

  • 1958: in Charles de Gaulle's referendum, Guinea alone voted no to staying in a French community. France pulled out at once, taking or wrecking much of its equipment as it went.
  • 1958 to 1984: Ahmed Sékou Touré ruled a one-party state; thousands died in its prison camps.
  • 1984: a military coup after his death.
  • 2010: first democratic election; a new coup came in 2021.

Guinea holds some of the largest bauxite reserves in the world. The N'Ko script for Manding languages was invented by a Guinean in 1949.
sum: Guinea is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, with its capital at Conakry. In 1958 it became the first French colony in Africa to vote itself free.
